title: Shape the Foundry player page
question: Which layout should carry forward? All three show the same example: Foundry is responding and the player can open it. These sketches choose a layout, not a working integration.

options.label: Quick entry
options.thesis: Status and Open Foundry share one compact row, with joining help underneath.
options.viewport: The Lobby header, Foundry title, one horizontal status-and-action strip, then optional help.
options.risk: Fast for returning players, but the status receives less emphasis.

options.label: One clear entrance
options.thesis: A single centered panel puts availability directly above Open Foundry.
options.viewport: The Lobby header frames a narrow central panel with status, one action and a short joining explanation.
options.risk: Uses more vertical space than the compact row for the same task.

options.label: Check, then join
options.thesis: Two connected steps distinguish checking availability here from joining inside Foundry.
options.viewport: A shared two-column area holds availability on the left and the Open Foundry action on the right; phones stack the steps.
options.risk: More explanation for first-time players adds structure to a task that returning players finish with one click.
